/v1/fees.policy: Lykia takes a protocol fee on every value-moving step (send, swap, FX, deposit, supply, borrow, bridge, Gateway deposit), paid on chain in the same transaction. Repay, withdrawals home, approvals, revokes and Tag steps are free.

beta.note: A hard cap above every Fence while Lykia's contracts are unaudited. Moves that bring value home are never capped.

routed.window: Intents kept by the API (30 days)

circle.basis: Circle products with a live or configured code path on this deployment (GET /v1/circle/status); not a usage count

sources.contracts: Deployments recorded by the owner console, each verified with eth_getCode
sources.accountsCreated: LykiaAccountFactory nonce on Arc minus one (one CREATE2 per account)
sources.memoSteps: Settled value-moving steps; each carries an Arc Memo with its verdict digest
sources.routed: Settled, priced steps of intents kept by the API

/v1/ecosystem?environment=mainnet.positioning: Built on Arc Network and Circle's products: the protocols on Arc mapped, the ones with an executable adapter routable on Lykia, and every agent inside its Fence.

directory.note: The official Arc ecosystem directory. This hub maps those protocols, marks each one routable, read-only or mapped on Lykia, and links each to its official entry.

protocols.name: Morpho Blue
protocols.summary: Isolated lending markets. Lykia borrows USDC (or EURC) against cirBTC on the 86% LLTV markets and keeps the health factor above the Fence floor.
protocols.evidence: morpho-org/sdks addresses.ts (ArcMainnet); markets from api.morpho.org (cirBTC/USDC 0xc2db…815d); supplyCollateral + borrow simulated with eth_call 2026-11-01

protocols.name: Aave V4
protocols.summary: Hub and Spoke lending. Main Spoke lends USDC, EURC, cirBTC and WETH; Forex Spoke pairs USDC and EURC. Lykia supplies, borrows and repays through the Spokes and reads the health factor on chain.
protocols.evidence: bgd-labs/aave-address-book AaveV4Arc.ts; Spoke implementation 0xf76b…ba79 ABI verified on Etherscan (chain 5042); supply/withdraw/borrow simulated via Multicall3From eth_call 2026-11-01; rates from api.aave.com

totals.summary: 14 protocols Lykia can route through today, plus 5 curators' vaults via Morpho · 95 protocols mapped on Arc

routed.window: Intents kept by the API (30 days)

circle.name: USDC and EURC
circle.lykia: Every plan settles in them; native (18) and ERC-20 (6) USDC handled as one balance.

circle.name: CCTP V2
circle.lykia: Intent bridges burn with Circle's Forwarding Service hook, so Circle mints on the destination; live fees per route (GET /v1/circle/cctp/fees) and transfer status (GET /v1/circle/cctp/status).

circle.name: CCTP Forwarding Service
circle.lykia: The intent engine's bridge step and POST /v1/circle/cctp/forward build depositForBurnWithHook with the forwarding hook; the step settles when Iris reports forwardState COMPLETE.

circle.name: Gateway (unified balance)
circle.lykia: Balance in the Flock, deposits in plans, and transfers out of Arc: maxFee from Gateway's /v1/estimate, burn intent to sign, then an unsigned gatewayMint, or forward: true for Circle's Forwarding Service to mint (GET /v1/circle/gateway/transfers/:id).

circle.name: Gateway Nanopayments (x402)
circle.lykia: Discovery shows which services take Gateway; vanilla x402 on Arc is paid through /v1/circle/x402 (owner or agent signs).

circle.name: Agent Marketplace discovery
circle.lykia: GET /v1/circle/services lists services an agent can pay for on Arc; Lyko can propose purchases inside the Fence.

circle.name: Developer-controlled wallets
circle.lykia: Opt-in for the operator: POST /v1/circle/wallets/agent provisions an SCA wallet bound to the signed-in address that created it; payouts can execute from it only for that address, after the Fence and the beta cap. The operator's entity secret signs, so this is a server-side signer, off unless LYKIA_CIRCLE_SERVER_WALLETS=true.

circle.name: Agent Wallets (Agent Stack)
circle.lykia: The default agent path: POST /v1/circle/policies/compile turns a Fence into the wallet's Circle spending policy (caps, allow and block lists) and the exact Circle CLI commands, and reports which rules Lykia's preflight enforces on top. Lykia cannot apply it: Circle requires the owner's OTP.

circle.name: Gas Station
circle.lykia: Agent wallets are created as SCA so a Gas Station policy can sponsor them; the profile's gas preference records the choice.

circle.name: Circle Paymaster
circle.lykia: Not needed on Arc: gas already is USDC. Circle Paymaster is not deployed on Arc (its v0.8 addresses have no code there, checked 2026-11-04); smart accounts on Arc fund their EntryPoint deposit in native USDC or use Gas Station.

circle.name: Compliance Engine screening
circle.lykia: External recipients are screened before planning; a DENIED address is added to the Fence's deny list, and an unscreened one is reported as such. Asks for ARC first and, if Circle refuses the chain, screens the same EVM address as ETH.

circle.name: StableFX
circle.lykia: Quote → taker signs the Permit2 typed data → trade → status (/v1/circle/stablefx/*). Without access, USDC↔EURC routes through Uniswap.

circle.name: USYC
circle.lykia: GET /v1/circle/usyc/eligibility reads the Entitlements contract; POST /v1/circle/usyc/prepare builds approve + deposit or redeem only for entitled wallets, with the Teller's preview and a Fence verdict (USYC must be an allowed token).

circle.name: Arc App Kit
circle.lykia: Client-side kits for your front end. Lykia sits beside them: check a plan with the Fence first, then call kit.send / swap / bridge; Circle-native server paths (CCTP, Gateway, StableFX) are Lykia execution providers.

x402.note: Circle's facilitator settles payments; this server has no Circle API key, so settlement is refused and the route keeps answering 402.

templates.title: Pay invoices
templates.summary: Transfers only, to payees you name. No swaps, no lending, no bridges.

templates.title: Trade small
templates.summary: USDC and EURC swaps on DEXs whose output the account can pin to itself, with a slippage cap.

templates.title: Earn
templates.summary: Deposit into and withdraw from Morpho vaults and Aave V4. Everything stays in the account.

templates.title: Custom
templates.summary: Your own Fence, narrowed to the leash's budget and expiry. It must sit inside the parent's Fence.

enforcement.how: LykiaAccount refuses every call after validUntil; the API stops the key at expiresAt.
On chain: perCall in token units per token (USDC 1:1, EURC at the reference rate when the leash was made). At the API: USD per step (caps.perStepUsd).
On chain: daily in token units over a rolling 24 h window. At the API: USD per day (caps.dailyUsd).
On chain: budget in token units over the session's life, charged up the whole session chain. At the API: USD over the leash's life.
On chain: agentTransfer only to the session's recipient list or the owner. At the API: the Fence's recipient allowlist.
agentExecute only on (target, selector) call rules, each pinning its output argument to the account; approve, transfer and permit selectors can never be allowlisted.
maxCalls on the session, counted on every node of the chain.
The API disables the key the moment you revoke; revokeSession on the account ends the session (and every sub-session) once signed.
The chain counts token units. Dollar amounts, prices and the beta cap are checked by the Fence at the API.
The Fence's venue list and the router's choice. On chain only the call rules exist, which are derived from these venues.
limits.maxSlippageBps sets the minimum output in the calldata. The chain does not compare prices.
Fence rules evaluated on every plan.

reasons.testnet: Spending from a Gateway balance is not switched on for Arc testnet yet.
reasons.mainnet: Spending from a Gateway balance is not switched on for Arc mainnet yet.

gateway.source: The part of the owner's Gateway balance deposited on Arc.

enforcement.how: LykiaStile refuses reservations after validUntil and stops validating its digests; the API stops the key at expiresAt.
On chain: perTransfer in USDC units, payment plus Lykia fee, never above the Stile's immutable ceiling ($100 while unaudited). At the API: USD per step.
On chain: daily over a rolling 24 h window, never above the Stile's ceiling ($300 while unaudited). At the API: USD per day.
On chain: lifetime on the session. At the API: USD over the leash's life.
On chain: the session's recipient list (32-byte addresses). At the API: the Fence's recipient allowlist.
On chain: the session's allowed Gateway domains. At the API: the leash's destination list.
Every reserved intent must debit the owner's deposit on Arc through Gateway Wallet, signed by the Stile, with empty hook data.
With a fee, a reservation is a burn intent set [payment, fee]: Gateway attests and mints both together or neither.
maxFee of each intent is at most the session's maxGatewayFee; Circle charges at most that.
The API disables the key at once; revokeSession on the Stile stops new reservations and validation. Gateway may validate against a block up to about 5 minutes old.

Gateway calls isValidSignature (read-only, in its validation enclave, with an RPC quorum); it answers only for reserved, unexpired, uncancelled digests of a live session while the Stile is not paused.
The Fence evaluates every transfer before the reservation is prepared.
